# Liquidation price formulas for shorts — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Liquidation price formulas for shorts. Run status: COMPLETED.

## How it works

- [statement] freqtrade is an open-source reference implementation of per-exchange liquidation formulas. Its Binance function uses the transcribed Binance formula with a tier rate and maintenance amount; its Bybit function uses the first-order form and refuses inverse contracts. Its documentation says it 'is able to calculate liquidation prices, but does not calculate liquidation fees', so liquidations 'will result in inaccurate profit/loss results for your bot', and cross-margin interactions may not be fully simulated. In backtests the Binance function falls back to each other trade's open rate where live runs use the mark price. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/leverage/ · keywords: Liquidation price formulas for shorts · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/develop/freqtrade/exchange/binance.py, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/develop/freqtrade/exchange/bybit.py

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] OKX does not publish a standalone futures liquidation price formula on the pages read. Its help page says position reduction or forced liquidation may be triggered when the maintenance margin ratio is at or below 100%, based on the mark price, and directs users to the built-in Futures Calculator (Liquidation Price tab). The calculator takes the pair, margin mode, direction, leverage, entry price, number of contracts and available margin. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-27) — https://www.okx.com/help/how-to-calculate-the-price-what-are-the-conditions-for-strong-flat · keywords: Liquidation price formulas for shorts · also: https://www.okx.com/help/liquidation-faq

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The liquidation price a venue displays is an estimate and can move. Hyperliquid: the figure shown while entering a trade can differ because book liquidity changes, and after opening it can still differ because of funding payments or changes in unrealized PnL of other cross positions. OKX: 'the estimated liquidation price is not the actual price at which liquidation will occur', and in USDT cross-margin mode it cannot be calculated when the account holds two or more USDT futures or leveraged positions in different pairs. KuCoin: in cross margin, positions are liquidated only when the risk ratio reaches 100%, and the cross liquidation price is 'for reference only'. freqtrade: cross-margin effects between positions may not be fully simulated outside live trading. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Liquidation price formulas for shorts · also: https://www.okx.com/help/liquidation-faq, https://www.kucoin.com/support/26694703491737, https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/leverage/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Liquidation triggers on a venue-defined reference price, not the last traded price. OKX: the liquidation price is based on the mark price, 'rather than the last price or the index price'. Hyperliquid: liquidations use a mark price that combines external CEX prices with Hyperliquid's book state. KuCoin: an isolated position enters liquidation when the mark price reaches the estimated liquidation price. dYdX: account value is estimated with the oracle price. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.okx.com/help/liquidation-faq · keywords: Liquidation price formulas for shorts · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations, https://www.kucoin.com/support/26694703491737, https://docs.dydx.xyz/concepts/trading/liquidations

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Inference from the tier rules: a short's notional rises as the price rises, so a large short can move into a higher-rate tier before it reaches the liquidation price that a flat-rate formula gives. A long's notional falls as its price falls, so the same tier effect works in its favour. Hyperliquid solves for the tier at the liquidation price; a flat-rate calculator does not, and so can overstate a large short's cushion. (medium confidence) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Liquidation price formulas for shorts · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margin-tiers, https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/b3c689c1f50a44cabb3a84e663b81d93
